incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 504s observed across EU and APAC regions for smart-routing traffic. Threshold breach: 6m aggregated error rate > 8%. Paging oncall.
Alex (oncall): on it. grabbing logs and checking paging runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/smart-routing
Maya (SRE): seeing a spike in 504 + backend connection resets from edge nodes. Correlating with recent fallback-policy push ~10:12 UTC.
Raj (runtime): pushed fallback-policy v2 yesterday that prefers cheaper model-variant in low-capacity zones. Could be selecting incompatible variant (different kv-cache layout).
Jon (DNS-SRE): also seeing increased DNS NXDOMAINs from a subset of resolver pools for eu-west and ap-southeast. TTLs look ok but a few edge NODATAs repeating.
Emily (support): getting customer tickets from two enterprise customers reporting generation timeouts and truncated responses.
Alex (oncall): quick mitigation options: 1) roll back fallback-policy to v1 2) force-route traffic to primary region 3) disable smart-routing entirely. Which low-risk first?
Maya (SRE): prefer rolling back policy first. rollback command in deploy bot: `/deploy rollback fallback-policy v2 -> v1` (requires approvals)
Raj (runtime): we can override routing decision at gateway: `route.override=primary-only` for affected product-keys. That avoids DNS churn.
Jon (DNS-SRE): while you decide, I'll start targeted DNS cache purge for eu-west edge (edge-cache-flush job) and increase monitoring of propagation. Command to run:
```
kubectl exec -n edge-tools dns-flusher -- --zone eu-west --nodes 12
```
Alex (oncall): rolling back fallback-policy now. @deploy-bot please run rollback. :pray:
incident-bot: deploy-bot triggered: `rollback fallback-policy v2 -> v1` by Alex (oncall). CI checks running.
Maya (SRE): CI passed. Applying rollback... :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Raj (runtime): while rollback applies, I'm issuing runtime override for product keys matching `prod_*` to primary-only to stop inter-region fallbacks.
Raj (runtime): override applied. Logs show routing decisions stabilizing for new requests. Latency dropping on eu-west API frontends.
Jon (DNS-SRE): edge cache purge started. Early telemetry shows fewer NODATAs from the subset of resolvers.
Emily (support): opening a customer impact summary for affected customers. Adding notes to status page draft.
Liz (product): please capture which model-variants were being selected by v2; we need to evaluate defaulting behavior. This caused degraded outputs for some prompts.
Maya (SRE): root cause hypothesis: fallback-policy v2 allowed cross-variant fallbacks to a quantized model lacking compatible KV-cache metadata -> runtime errors -> 504. DNS propagation issues amplified retries and routing instability.
Alex (oncall): current status: rollback complete, routing override in place, edge flush running. Error rate down from 8.3% -> 1.1% over 15m.
Raj (runtime): disabling automatic cross-variant fallback until we add compatibility checks in runtime. I'll open PR for gating logic.
Jon (DNS-SRE): edge flush finished; verified RRsets for eu-west/ap-southeast are stable and resolvers returning expected A records.
Emily (support): status page published: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1815002468, customers notified via email for impacted accounts.
Liz (product): tracking action items: (1) compatibility guard in runtime (owner: Raj) (2) fail-safe in fallback-policy config to prevent cross-architecture variants (owner: Product) (3) improve DNS-propagation observability for smart-routing (owner: Jon)
Maya (SRE): handing off to night oncall. Please monitor for 2 hours and escalate if error rate > 2% or latency spikes.
Alex (oncall): thanks all. Handoff notes in #oncall-handoffs. Signing off from active page at 1815004968. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated) — follow-ups open in #incidents-postmortem. Reference: runbook link and PRs.
